races.name: Wexford Town Mares Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a poor recent string (772U7) including an unseating; Timothy Doyle yard at 0/9 in 14 days and amateur Mr D Doyle rides — 10 days since last run keeps her fresh but form does not suggest she can bridge the gap from the back on Good ground here.

runners_data.name: Farfromnowhere
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's 8-year-old has solid Good-ground credentials (7/10 similar going) and is the only genuine pace-setter in this field; the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild discount but she still dictates by default — the question is whether she can maintain it after the final fence rather than track.

runners_data.name: Full Of Life
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's mare won a 1m7f chase on Good ground and is proven at this trip, but 85 days off is a concern and she is a natural front-runner displaced to a tracking role by the pace map — De Bromhead at 5/30 in 14 days provides stable confidence, and Darragh O'Keeffe is an astute partner if she can settle.

runners_data.name: Future Prospect
runners_data.note: Mullins-Townend combination is always a major flag, and the mare is 2W5P on similar going; genuinely wants to race up with the pace but, like Full Of Life, her natural position is squeezed by Farfromnowhere — if she accepts a second or third slot she remains a serious threat, particularly off a 22-day break.

runners_data.name: Kaylasjet
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and going preference entirely unknown (UNKNOWN tag); a string of pulled-up finishes (PP4-P) and a 7lb apprentice for a yard at 0/1 in 14 days makes her very hard to assess — only consider if significant market support emerges closer to the off.

runners_data.name: La Note Verte
runners_data.note: Won two of her last five on Good ground with strong course-going consistency (6/7 similar going, 3W4P) and JJ Slevin is an excellent jumps jockey for Mullins; 74 days off is the one query, but the form profile — including a recent third — suggests she is the most natural beneficiary of a tracking role just off Farfromnowhere's fractions.

races.paceDynamic: Farfromnowhere is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for that position, will control the tempo from the outset on Good ground at Wexford over 1m7½f. The pace is likely to be honest but manageable — Farfromnowhere's STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects she is racing slightly out of role at this prominent-to-lead end, yet she still represents the only horse likely to dictate. The field holds more prominent types than the race can accommodate: Future Prospect, Full Of Life, and La Note Verte all have the profile to race prominently, but with Farfromnowhere already committed to the front, at least two of these must concede ground and race further back than ideal, with La Note Verte — the most course-ground-consistent of the trio — best placed to secure the prime stalking slot. A truly contested pace is not expected, which tilts the tactical advantage toward a well-positioned tracking horse who can travel economically in second or third and produce a clean jump at the final fence — the prominent-to-mid profile that can settle yet sustain is the race shape to be with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clean Lead, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Farfromnowhere controls an uncontested pace and a prominent tracking horse follows economically throughout.
scenarios.body: Farfromnowhere sets a regulated tempo with no pressure, allowing a close-tracking rival to conserve energy before asserting from the second-last; clean jumping and Good ground rewards the horse that best combines jumping fluency with sustained galloping ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Farfromnowhere's pace is truly conservative and she jumps flawlessly, never giving rivals a target to attack.
scenarios.body: An unchallenged, slow-build tempo means Farfromnowhere is never off the bridle until deep in the straight, and if her rivals are slow to respond or jump poorly at the last, she stays in front on the Good surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Falls Apart, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Farfromnowhere makes an early jumping error or fades from three out, releasing the race for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Beauforts Storm, held up off an undemanding early gallop, could find late momentum if the race deteriorates into chaos at the business end; however, her recent form (772U7) makes conversion unlikely even in a favourable shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Kaylasjet, unknown on going and lightly raced, produces a career-best and outjumps the field throughout.
scenarios.body: With no reliable form read on Good ground, Kaylasjet is a complete wildcard — Ben Kennedy (7lb claimer) takes the ride for a yard with minimal recent strike rate, and while an upset is possible it requires too many unknowns aligning.

watchPoints.text: Watch La Note Verte's jumping from the third-last — if she travels fluently behind Farfromnowhere with Slevin patient, she is the most dangerous at the business end given her Going and course consistency.

Farfromnowhere's sectionals bear monitoring: if she is ridden aggressively from the outset rather than rolling along, she could empty from two out and gift the race to a tracker — Paul Nolan's runners can be front-run boldly.

Future Prospect and Full Of Life may clash for position early as both want to be prominent — any early scrimmaging between them could compromise both and shuffle one back to an uncomfortable settling position behind their natural style.

Kaylasjet is completely unknown on Good ground and with a 7lb claimer aboard; any significant market move before the off should be noted as stable information may exist that the form book cannot reveal.

Beauforts Storm's rider Mr D Doyle (7lb claim) gives the yard a weight advantage, but the unseating on recent form warrants caution — monitor her at the early fences before drawing any conclusions about her jumping confidence.

races.name: Wexfordraces.ie Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Centreofattention
runners_data.note: E Bolger's seven-year-old carries modest recent form (/60-8P) and zero wins or places on similar going in five comparable runs; a natural hold-up horse whose instinct will be to race even further back than the midfield map position suggests, making a winning effort in this expected moderate-tempo shape very hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Coul Dreamer
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for W McCreery returning just eight days after a run, with one win from fifteen similar-going starts — naturally wants to be ridden from the rear but may creep closer in a slowly-run race; recent flat form on good ground (4th, 4th) is consistent if unspectacular and the short turnaround is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Jet Setting Jim
runners_data.note: The key pace-setter: Phillip Enright takes over on Andrew Slattery's nine-year-old who has 13 runs from 15 on similar going and was placed four times at this trip, but returns after a 294-day absence which is the single biggest question mark against a bold front-running display.

runners_data.name: Killeemore Lad
runners_data.note: Cian Quirke partners Andrew Slattery's eight-year-old who has been off 745 days — a significant absence — yet owns excellent form figures of 1-2-2-2 at this trip and going combination; a true hold-up horse who will be produced late, and the extreme layoff is the only credible reason to oppose him if the gallop quickens.

runners_data.name: Silent Selector
runners_data.note: Philip Donovan rides Gerard O'Leary's six-year-old, a natural hold-up horse with two wins from thirteen similar-going runs and course form over this trip; last seen 19 days ago finishing 5th, and the pattern of running suggests she needs a testing gallop to show her best.

runners_data.name: Sky Lord
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old (De Bromhead T14: 5/30) wears a tongue-strap and cheekpieces, has shown consistency (3rd-3rd-4th in recent chases) but has just four runs from eleven on comparable going and only one placed effort — a hold-up horse who is capable on his day but needs the race to be run to suit him.

runners_data.name: Where Are You Now
runners_data.note: Charlie O'Dwyer (3lb claimer) partners E Bolger's five-year-old, a prominent-going type who will push forward to track Jet Setting Jim but whose form string (62-67P) and zero wins or places from five comparable-going starts raises questions about ability to sustain the effort when challenged.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: Daniel King rides David Harry Kelly's seven-year-old who has a win and three places from five similar-going starts — the best record of the prominent-going types — and a recent second on comparable going 22 days ago; a straightforward prominent racer whose jumping consistency will be the deciding factor if Jet Setting Jim comes back to the field.

races.paceDynamic: Jet Setting Jim is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner beginners' chase and, coming off a 294-day absence, Andrew Slattery's nine-year-old will nonetheless attempt to dictate from the front over 1m7½f on good ground at Wexford — a track that rewards horses who can travel comfortably and jump fluently in a rhythm. With no genuine rival willing to pressurise him early, he should secure an uncontested lead and set a measured, sustainable gallop, meaning the race is unlikely to develop into a true stamina test and the emphasis will fall on jumping accuracy and a turn of foot from two out. Where Are You Now and William Tell are the other prominent-going types and will push forward to track Jet Setting Jim, ensuring there is a small group disputing the lead without the pace becoming truly brutal. This shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or at least travel close to the pace and produce a clean jumping round, as the expected moderate tempo will not suit those needing a genuinely strong gallop to be delivered late. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Centreofattention, Coul Dreamer, and Killeemore Lad are all natural hold-up horses but have been redistributed to midfield in the map; of those three, Killeemore Lad's course-and-distance profile and Coul Dreamer's recent form make them most likely to manoeuvre forward in practice, though none will land in their ideal position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jet Setting Jim Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Jet Setting Jim jumps fluently from the front and sets a controlled, uncontested gallop that denies closers a searching test.
scenarios.body: Jet Setting Jim, unchallenged on the front end, controls the tempo and jumps his way to victory, with Where Are You Now and William Tell the closest pursuers simply unable to reel him in when he quickens from the second-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Drive Home
scenarios.trigger: If Jet Setting Jim is reeled in from three out and the race develops into a battle between the prominent-tracking horses.
scenarios.body: William Tell or Where Are You Now looms up to challenge Jet Setting Jim from the third-last, turning it into a jumping duel up the home straight where accuracy and fitness under pressure decide the outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and one of the hold-up types finds clear running to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Killeemore Lad, with excellent form figures at this trip and going, or Sky Lord for Henry De Bromhead, pick their way through a tiring field if the gallop is genuinely searching — but this scenario is less likely given the expected moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Jet Setting Jim makes a jumping error or fades sharply, causing the race to collapse into a scramble in the home straight.
scenarios.body: A messy finish with multiple horses in with a chance approaching the last, favouring whichever horse has been produced widest and freshest — Silent Selector's course-winning form and Sky Lord's consistency make them the most likely beneficiaries in chaos.

watchPoints.text: Jet Setting Jim's 294-day absence is the single biggest danger flag — if he blunders or weakens sharply after a long lay-off, the entire race shape collapses and William Tell or Where Are You Now inherit the race from prominent positions.

Killeemore Lad returns from 745 days off and, while his form figures over this trip and going are outstanding, extreme absence makes him a watch in the early fences — any jumping hesitancy from ring-rustiness would end his chance of producing a trademark late run.

With three redistributed hold-up horses (Centreofattention, Coul Dreamer, Killeemore Lad) all likely trying to creep closer in a moderate pace, watch for traffic congestion and interference on the final bend if the field bunches behind Jet Setting Jim.

Where Are You Now's three-pound claimer Charlie O'Dwyer is worth monitoring at the early fences — in a beginners' chase, an inexperienced combination prominent in the race could cause issues for those immediately behind if a mistake is made.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Trasna Na Pairce
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with Henry De Bromhead in form (5/30 T14); 12 of 14 runs on similar going yielded 2 wins and 5 places, so the Good surface is squarely in her favour — she is tagged here as a prominent type but this is exactly the horse most likely to lead and she should be allowed to do so unchallenged.

runners_data.name: Mercury Mission
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with five of last five runs on Good or similar and three wins among them at around this distance; Paul Cluskey's yard is quiet (0/1 T14) but this horse is in its element at 1m7½f on Good and can realistically sit second throughout.

runners_data.name: Tuckmill
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old who has been off 83 days and whose form string (/0P70-) is largely uninspiring; Peter Fahey sends him here with a tongue-strap and he is prominent in style, though the layoff and moderate recent form are genuine concerns at this level.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer who has recorded three placed efforts from just six runs on Good ground — a genuinely clean record for the surface; she needs others to set a strong enough pace and Patrick O'Brien's booking is workmanlike, but she is the truest closer in the field.

runners_data.name: Tequila Talkin'
runners_data.note: Front-running instincts mean Alan O'Sullivan (claimer) will likely find this horse uncomfortable to place — it wants to be prominent but the race map has little room for it; its two most recent runs (3rd and 2nd) on Good ground show ability, but the role mismatch is the key handicap.

runners_data.name: Stoneyford Lady
runners_data.note: Won over 1m7½f on Good and was runner-up in similar conditions, so the trip and surface are fine; Henry De Bromhead runs three here (T14:5/30), but Stoneyford Lady's natural prominence means Danny Power (claimer) will face an early positioning puzzle with a crowded prominent rail.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been on Good ground at 2m or beyond, and the drop to 1m7½f is a shortening that may not entirely suit a horse whose style profile says it wants to stride on — Joshua Halford's claim helps the weight, but P J Rothwell's yard is modestly in form (1/21 T14) and the horse will likely find itself racing a length or two off its preferred spot.

races.paceDynamic: Trasna Na Pairce is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to push her hard from the outset, she should be able to control matters from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m7½f trip on Good ground at Wexford. Mercury Mission and Tuckmill are the most credible prominent challengers who can realistically track her, while Tequila Talkin', Stoneyford Lady, and Ballybrittas are all natural prominent types who will be squeezed back into midfield roles against their instincts because this field simply cannot accommodate five horses racing up with the pace. With the tempo likely to be honest but uncontested, Trasna Na Pairce dictates the race on her own terms, and the race shape strongly favours horses who can either lead or sit a close, economical second — a controlled, front-running scenario is the dominant shape here, and genuine hold-up horses like Lady Doyanne will need others to press Trasna Na Pairce into overdrive to get a true test. Of the crowded prominent brigade, Mercury Mission and Tuckmill are best placed to actually secure the positions closest to the pace; Tequila Talkin', Stoneyford Lady, and Ballybrittas are unlikely to get their natural spot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trasna Na Pairce Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce bowls along uncontested at a fair but controlled clip and none of the redistributed prominent types can work close enough to apply pressure.
scenarios.body: She sets a sustainable pace that suits her stamina profile, and with no rival forcing her hand the race becomes a test of who can travel most efficiently close to the front — a format that flatters the leader and her nearest tracker Mercury Mission.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Mercury Mission or Tuckmill press Trasna Na Pairce from early enough to give her a genuine race and the pace lifts into a true test of jumping and staying.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run gallop exposes any weakness in the leader, and horses who can race prominently with fluency over fences and sustain their effort to the last are rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight after a steady early tempo, allowing Lady Doyanne or a recovering midfield runner to swoop.
scenarios.body: A moderate overall fractions scenario is exactly what hold-up horses need, and Lady Doyanne's consistent Good-ground form figures and strong finishing profile make her the likeliest beneficiary if the front end tires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types — Tequila Talkin', Stoneyford Lady, or Ballybrittas — push hard for position early and create an unexpectedly strong pace that scrambles the field.
scenarios.body: A contested early tempo would burn out several prominent types and potentially leave the race open to whoever travels widest or steadiest — an untidy scenario that produces a messy result.

watchPoints.text: Trasna Na Pairce sets the pace alone — watch whether Mercury Mission or Tuckmill can track her closely enough to apply jumping pressure at the later fences, because if they do the leader's stamina will be genuinely tested.

Tequila Talkin', Stoneyford Lady, and Ballybrittas are all natural prominent types loaded into a single race — watch the opening furlong for a scramble for position that could unsettle all three and create a chaotic early shape.

Lady Doyanne's finishing kick depends entirely on the gallop being genuine enough to stretch the prominent horses — if Trasna Na Pairce idles in front on Good ground, the closer's opportunity may simply not materialise.

Tuckmill has been off 83 days with a modest form string; watch his jumping early as a ten-year-old returning from a break can be rusty at the fences, and any blunder could compromise his position for a horse that needs to be up with the pace.

Henry De Bromhead saddles three runners (Trasna Na Pairce, Lady Doyanne, Stoneyford Lady) — watch for any tactical stable communication between Dylan Whelan and Patrick O'Brien that might see the hold-up horse given a lead by the yard's front-runner.

races.name: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Farrokh
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here; has solid Wexford course form at this trip on good ground (2/17f/GOO) and should get an uncontested lead, but 244-day absence is a real concern and Connell's stable is 0/1 in the past fortnight — straightforward leader who may just need the run.

runners_data.name: Keep On Dreaming
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden in the saddle is a significant booking for this Bolger-trained six-year-old; hold-up style suits a race where Farrokh will set a retrievable pace, but limited recent good-going form (only 2 from 5 similar-ground runs in the sim) and a slightly awkward trip profile temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Justicialism
runners_data.note: Has been remarkably consistent in this grade, placing in four of his last five with a tongue-tie today; true hold-up horse who relishes good ground (8/15 sim-going) and handles this trip well, and the 26-day turnaround is ideal — his profile is that of a horse who keeps arriving without ever quite winning.

runners_data.name: Arctic Piper
runners_data.note: 195 days off the track is the obvious flag, and his best form has come on Heavy/Soft ground rather than Good; a genuine hold-up type whose Wexford return looks like a prep run rather than a winning pitch.

runners_data.name: Quinn The Eskimo
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie applied; has a win at this trip on good ground but his recent string of pullings-up and unfinished runs (two U/P in last six) demands respect — hold-up style in a field with limited pace to chase could leave him cold.

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: Won his most recent start (1/16f/GOO) and has five career wins on good ground; though the map places him in midfield, he is a horse who has raced prominently when conditions allow and the pace data note confirms he is likely to push forward — strong form angle with headgear (p) already applied.

runners_data.name: L'Amiral Fromentin
runners_data.note: Second last time out (2/16f/GOO) for the in-form Rothwell yard (1/21 T14); a natural hold-up horse by trade but the redistribution note acknowledges he may push closer than the map suggests — Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking and the trip/going combination suits.

runners_data.name: King's Son
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who finished third last time (3/20f/GOO) at a longer trip; JJ Slevin takes the ride which upgrades his claims sharply — the 19-day gap is fine and good ground at 1m7½f is exactly the profile this horse has been placed over before.

runners_data.name: Getaway Henry
runners_data.note: Won 12 days ago (1/16f/GOO) so is very much in form and his two career wins have both come on good ground; prominent style and a in-form yard makes him interesting, though stepping up from 16f to 15f is a slight query and the 5lb claim from Kenneally is a small offset.

runners_data.name: Only A Dollar
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by profile; recent form is modest (5th and 0 last time) and his best good-ground run was a fifth — the redistribution note means he is unlikely to get a perfect position, further dampening his chances in this field.

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placing form on good ground (three top-3 finishes in last five); form has tailed off lately (8th, 5th) and she is unproven beyond 18f — the step up to 1m7½f on a track that can stretch stamina is a concern.

runners_data.name: Dunany Point
runners_data.note: Hasn't finished closer than sixth in his last five, including a pull-up; prominent by style but the form line is deeply uninspiring and the 53-day break adds little confidence — likely to need to improve markedly to factor.

runners_data.name: Dontdooddson
runners_data.note: Veteran of 13 seasons and has been a consistent seventh in his last three runs on good ground; mapped to midfield because the field is overloaded with prominent types ahead of him and, with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93, his chance in any shape where he gets his natural position looks remote at this stage of his career.

races.paceDynamic: Farrokh is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to match him stride-for-stride, he should be able to slide into a comfortable, controlled lead from the outset on good ground at Wexford. Behind him, King's Son, Getaway Henry, Polly Poppins and Dunany Point are all legitimate prominent types who will compete for the seats directly behind, meaning the early positions from second to fifth could be fractious even if the overall tempo is not searingly fast. The natural hold-up horses — Keep On Dreaming, Justicialism, Quinn The Eskimo and Arctic Piper — should settle towards the rear without fuss, but Dontdooddson, Chosen Shant, L'Amiral Fromentin and Only A Dollar are true prominent or hold-up types who have been pushed back on the map because there is simply insufficient room in the front half of this 13-runner field for all of them; of these, Chosen Shant and L'Amiral Fromentin are most likely to push forward and actually contest a midfield berth given their recent tactical form. With Farrokh setting a sustainable, uncontested tempo and good ground rewarding horses that travel smoothly and jump well, this race shape distinctly favours prominent racers who can track the leader without burning energy and pounce at the second-last — not true hold-up types who face a longer run from the rear with no pace collapse to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Farrokh Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Farrokh leads at a fair but unhurried gallop and the prominent horses behind track comfortably to the final fence.
scenarios.body: Farrokh dictates without being pressured and the race sets up perfectly for a horse travelling in second or third to pounce jumping the last on good ground; the measured pace means hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up in the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Steadies, Hold-Up Horses Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Farrokh crawls early, the field concertinas and the pace only quickens from the third-last, giving hold-up horses a chance to close.
scenarios.body: A truly slow early tempo can compress the field enough that Keep On Dreaming or Justicialism, tucked in behind, find the pace quickening into their strengths late; good ground suits those who stay on powerfully rather than sprint, and both have strong recent form finishing second or better.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack chases Farrokh hard, sets a strong pace and the leaders are spent entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Should several prominent types push forward and force Farrokh into a contested gallop, the race could set up for the true closers to swoopfrom the rear; Keep On Dreaming and Justicialism, both proven at the trip on good going, are best placed to capitalise on a pace collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Farrokh Leads All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If Farrokh gets a completely uncontested lead and the prominent horses behind fail to mount a serious challenge jumping the last.
scenarios.body: On a tight flat track like Wexford with good ground and a solo controlled tempo, a front-runner left entirely alone can be very difficult to reel in; Farrokh has the form (second on this course at this trip in similar conditions) to simply stay on and hold every challenger.

watchPoints.text: Farrokh's 244-day layoff is a genuine danger flag — if he has trained off at home or lacks fitness, the entire race shape loses its anchor and the pace scenario becomes chaotic with multiple prominent types scrapping for the lead.

King's Son with JJ Slevin is the standout jockey upgrade in the race — watch for him being sent forward aggressively from the off to secure a prominent pitch, which could apply more pressure to Farrokh than the pace map currently implies.

Chosen Shant won last time out on identical going and trip; his redistribution to midfield may be academic if he bounces forward from the draw — his presence near the pace would shift scenario probabilities toward a stronger gallop.

Getaway Henry runs just 12 days after a win, and trainer Daniel O'Leary has no runners in the T14 window — monitor market moves, as a fit, in-form prominent horse on a quick turnaround in a competitive handicap can be overlooked at a price.

L'Amiral Fromentin's booking of Darragh O'Keeffe is worth tracking — O'Keeffe rarely rides without a live chance and the horse's recent second on identical good ground at the same trip puts him in the frame if the pace sets up for a late challenge.

races.name: Wexford Quay Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Boston Jury
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's hold-up performer with Jack Kennedy up, showing eight placings from ten tries on similar Good ground (sim-going 8/10, 1W2P); needs a truly run race to get competitive late and the likely steady pace is a mild concern, though the class angle is live.

runners_data.name: Figurehead
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old on a long losing run (0W2P in sim-going, last of 16 twice on Good), trainer rated 0/1 in the 14-day window; tongue-tie and visor suggest connections are searching for a solution and he is hard to support on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Glenashling
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up type has placed on Good ground before (OR 116, best in the field); the 45-day break and tongue-tie are worth noting, but Keith Donoghue is a strong booking and he handles this surface well enough to be competitive if the race develops into a stamina test.

runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good at this sort of trip but has also pulled up and finished well back recently (form: 110-P7); a natural prominent racer who will struggle to get to the front with this many rivals wanting to go forward — the style-fit discount of 0.92 is meaningful here.

runners_data.name: Kool One
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer with a clean record on Good (sim-going 6/15, 3W3P) for Conor Maxwell; the 59-day break is the one query, but he is lightly raced, should get a clear run from his likely early position, and the step up in trip over 2m3f suits.

runners_data.name: Los Blanco
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead has him fit after 84 days (5/30 in T14 window) and Darragh O'Keeffe is a polished booking; won on Good and placed on Soft, has finished 1st and 2nd at this sort of distance, and should be able to sit just off the leader cleanly — one of the most straightforward profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for Denis Hogan, placed on Good at 2m (sim-going 3/14, 0W1P — no wins on Good is a flag); Daniel King takes the mount and the horse has finished 2nd twice recently but needs to improve his Good-ground record to feature.

runners_data.name: Now So Jake
runners_data.note: Returning from a 720-day layoff (last ran January 2023), which is the dominant factor; won over 3m and placed at 2m3f when last seen, and the form before injury reads well, but fitness on comeback from almost two years off is deeply uncertain.

runners_data.name: West Away
runners_data.note: Eoghan Finegan (5lb claim) takes the mount for a trainer rated 1/1 in the 14-day window; a natural prominent racer who is mapped to midfield due to the crowded pace picture — the 208-day absence compounds the style-fit concern and his recent form (20P76) does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Clody Diamond
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's runner carries a 7lb pull in the weights (159lbs) and has a placing on Good at 2m; in truth he wants to race forward but the congested pace map means that position may not be available — his best run on Good came when second at 2m, so the trip and surface are workable if he can find daylight.

runners_data.name: Colleen Danu
runners_data.note: Simon Torrens rides Patrick Foley's mare who won on Good at 2m and has placed multiple times on this surface (sim-going 9/15, 3W4P); naturally wants to race prominently but is one of several types mapped back from her ideal spot — the lighter weight (159lbs) is a genuine plus if she can get close enough to the pace.

runners_data.name: Queenofthelodge
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright takes over on Sheila Curling's six-year-old who carries the 'p' headgear flag for the first time; the sole confirmed front-runner in the race, though the style-fit tag (0.92) reflects that this is not a natural front-runner's course shape — on Good she has been placed regularly and the unchallenged lead is a real asset if she retains enough for the run-in.

races.paceDynamic: Queenofthelodge is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a style-fit tag of 0.92, is expected to bowl along in front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m3f — no serious rival will push her early, so the tempo should be measured rather than punishing. The prominent contingent is severely overcrowded: Jackson Lamb, Colleen Danu, Clody Diamond, and West Away are all natural front-runners or prominent racers redistributed to midfield because the map cannot place them all in their preferred slot — only Los Blanco, Kool One, Mickie Angel, and Now So Jake can realistically sit where they want. With Queenofthelodge likely to control from the front at a steady clip and several prominent types unable to secure their natural berth, the race will string out early in the back straight as the congestion resolves, before the real race ignites from three out. This shape — a single unhurried pace-setter, a compacted midfield, and a genuine stamina test over 2m3f on Good — strongly favours genuine prominent racers who land in a forward position cleanly, with the ability to jump and travel fluently rather than sit in a pocket and wait.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Queenofthelodge Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Queenofthelodge dictates a steady gallop unchallenged and the true prominent horses (Los Blanco, Kool One, Now So Jake) travel smoothly just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Queenofthelodge sets a comfortable tempo, the field fans out from the third-last, and horses positioned 2nd–4th have first run on the leaders jumping the last; this shape rewards good jumpers with tactical speed who can quicken off a sound surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Increase Mid-Race, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group creates pressure mid-race as Jackson Lamb or Colleen Danu attempt to recover their natural forward position, lifting the tempo.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop from halfway means only genuine stayers with real reserves see out the 2m3f, penalising those who have had to race keen chasing position; hold-up horses with strong finishes get competitive late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Queenofthelodge Stays Upsides, Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Queenofthelodge's rivals fail to lay down a sustained challenge and she is left to stride on uncollected from two out.
scenarios.body: On Good ground over this trip, a front-runner allowed to coast at her own pace can repel ralliers who are stuck in traffic or unable to accelerate quickly enough off a flat track; the winner is the horse that jumps best under no pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution logjam causes early jostling that burns off several prominent types, leaving the hold-up horses with a genuine target.
scenarios.body: Boston Jury (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) and Glenashling (Keith Donoghue, Gavin Cromwell) would be the primary beneficiaries of a muddled race that sets up for a late rattle; however this shape is inherently less likely given the field lacks true front-runners who will force a breakneck pace.

watchPoints.text: Los Blanco and Kool One — if either secures an uncontested 2nd or 3rd on the fence behind Queenofthelodge from the off, they will be very hard to peg back turning for home on this Good ground.

Jackson Lamb, Colleen Danu, Clody Diamond and West Away — all natural prominent types who cannot all get their position; watch the early exchanges for barging and potential interference as they compete for the same real estate, which could unsettle several runners.

Now So Jake — 720-day absence makes fitness impossible to gauge from the form book; if he travels fluently early he is interesting on old form, but a conspicuous backward move before three out should be treated as a fitness flag rather than a tactical move.

Glenashling — Keith Donoghue often drops hold-up horses in from the back at Wexford and makes a late move; watch how far back he is at the halfway point, as a position more than eight lengths off the pace on this flat track would likely be too much to make up.

Queenofthelodge's jumping — as the lone front-runner on a beginners' chase card, any jumping error from her at an early fence could immediately change the race shape and bring the prominent pack into play a circuit earlier than expected.

races.name: WTW Willis Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Nastya
runners_data.note: Won three of last four over 3m on Good at Wexford-equivalent trips for De Bromhead, 62 days off but proven fresh; the lone confirmed front-runner who will dictate tempo, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a formality here as leading is exactly her role — she is the one horse guaranteed her natural position.

runners_data.name: Caesar Rock
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with a striking five-run streak of placed efforts and a 11/15 sim-going record on Good; races prominently under an apprentice claim and is the model of consistency, though the lack of a recent win and weight of 164lbs over 3m½f are the questions.

runners_data.name: Goody Four Shoes
runners_data.note: Won over 3m2f on Good just 44 days ago for Gibney; junior rider Harry Sexton (7) is the query over this longer test but the horse's recent course-distance victory is impossible to ignore and he handles Good ground comfortably.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Only six years old and still progressing, trained by Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy in the saddle — the most potent jockey-trainer combination in the field; raced 12 days ago so bounce risk exists, but his sim-going record (10/14 on Good) and consistent placed runs suggest he will travel into the race smoothly from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Astley
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator under Alex Harvey, the only horse in the race who is naturally at home coming from off the bridle; five-run winless streak and 79 days off are dual concerns, but the authentic style at least means he will be racing in his own role unlike several rivals.

runners_data.name: Teenage Kiss
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the mount on this five-year-old who won over 3m on Good last time and has strong sim-going stats (9/12); his natural instinct is to race prominently but the crowded lead group means he is mapped to midfield — Cobden's tactical nous gives him the best chance among the displaced prominent types of still securing a forward position.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Recent form reads PP-657 and the horse has struggled in similar company over 24f on Good; though a genuine front-runner by nature, he cannot get to the front in this field and the redistribution to midfield compounds an already difficult profile — trainer T14 figures (1/21) offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Duty Bound
runners_data.note: Won twice from 15 Good-ground runs in similar company and has experience over this trip; a natural front-runner for J P Flavin who will be squeezed into midfield by the sheer volume of pace in this field, and racing against instinct over 3m½f is an uncomfortable ask — the 22-day turnaround is fine but the style mismatch is the real concern.

runners_data.name: Ceroc
runners_data.note: Placed at 26f on Good last time out (2/26f/GOO) and has a 11/15 sim-going record, but seven placed efforts without a win tells its own story; another front-runner by nature who ends up mapped to midfield, and at OR=102 is the lowest-rated runner — Phillip Enright's experience helps but the combination of style displacement and class deficit is a tough hand.

races.paceDynamic: Nastya is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she will stride into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the off over this 3m½f trip on Good ground at Wexford. The pace will be honest but controlled — Nastya has won three of her last four starts from the front and De Bromhead's mare is not going to be hurried into setting a suicidal tempo. Caesar Rock, Scalpnagoon, and Goody Four Shoes will attempt to track prominently behind her, creating a compact lead group, but several others — Teenage Kiss, Dorans Law, Duty Bound, and Ceroc — are genuine prominent types who cannot all get their preferred position and will be forced to race further back than ideal. This field holds more front-running and prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate: of those pushed back, Teenage Kiss and Scalpnagoon are the most likely to still secure a forward berth given their natural tactical speed and jockey quality (Cobden, Kennedy). The resulting shape favours horses who can travel prominently in the first three or four, conserve energy behind a steady gallop, and produce a sustained jumping run from the home turn — true prominent racers who secure their slot will be at a clear advantage over those forced wide or into hold-up mode against their will.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nastya Controls, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Nastya bowls along uncontested and the pace is measured enough that the lead group stays intact over the final two fences.
scenarios.body: Nastya sets a comfortable gallop, the field strings out into a rhythm, and those racing in the first three or four — particularly Caesar Rock and Scalpnagoon — travel sweetly before challenging at the last; the Good ground and long trip reward those who conserve energy in a prominent position rather than making up ground from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Nastya's gallop is just steady enough for a well-placed tracker to outstay her up the straight.
scenarios.body: Scalpnagoon or Caesar Rock, both proven in Good conditions at this sort of trip, sit two lengths off the pace and produce a clean round of jumping to wear Nastya down from the home turn; their consistency and solid sim-going records make either capable of overtaking a front-runner who has been asked to do a lot of donkey work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Runner Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly early, stringing the field out and creating room for a prominent type forced rearward to make ground through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Teenage Kiss or Duty Bound, both natural front-runners who lose several lengths at the start of the race against their instincts, find themselves with a clear run as others tire and close from mid-division; however, both carry a STYLE_FIT discount and racing out of role at this marathon trip on Good ground is a significant ask.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set the race up for a closer coming from well off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Astley, the only genuine hold-up type in the field, gets a dream tow into the race if the prominent contingent burn each other out; the 79-day absence and modest recent form (7535-5) make it hard to rely on, but the style is authentic and Alex Harvey would inherit a clear run if the field fractures.

watchPoints.text: Watch Scalpnagoon at the first few fences — if Jack Kennedy pushes him forward aggressively to claim a prominent pitch, he could disrupt the intended rhythm of Nastya and reorder the entire lead group.

Teenage Kiss under Harry Cobden bears monitoring in the early stages: if Cobden senses daylight he may attempt to push forward into his natural position, creating a pocket of scrimmaging behind Nastya across the first mile.

Caesar Rock's apprentice rider (Joshua Halford, 7) is the clearest jockey downgrade in the race — watch whether he can keep the horse balanced and prominent at the fences without losing ground on the turns, which would be costly in a race where position is already at a premium.

Dorans Law pulled up twice recently and his jumping reliability is a live safety concern in a nine-runner field where several horses are conceding their natural position — a mistake or refusal from him in the back straight could cause significant interference.

Nastya's last run was 62 days ago — monitor her behaviour in the parade ring and at the start; if she races freely into the first few fences rather than settling, the pace could be quicker than anticipated and open the race up for closers.

races.name: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Embrace The Day
runners_data.note: A five-year-old prominent runner for Gavin Cromwell and Keith Donoghue, who carries a fade flag in the finish — her recent form of 884-51 shows she can win but the finish concern over 3m½f on Good ground is a real caveat; 53 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Midnight Moonshine
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone pace-setter here, though the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag indicates she is racing out of her most comfortable role — her recent form of 3F-090 and a sim-going record of 13/15 places without a win in similar conditions suggest she may set it up for others.

runners_data.name: North Of Nashville
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent runner for Colin Bowe and Ricky Doyle with course form that reads well — won over 26f on Good and has two wins and two places from 15 similar-going runs; the best-credentialed front-rank horse behind Moonshine.

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Noel C Kelly, aged ten, with a solid sim-going record of 12/15 and one win on Good — Conor Stone-Walsh keeps the ride and the staying trip suits a horse who races patiently.

runners_data.name: Anodandawink
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the mount for Ciaran Murphy on this five-year-old prominent type, but the fade flag and a form line of 003-92 — including a recent ninth — raises doubts about whether he can see out this trip, even off a handy mark of OR=93.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Remarkably lightly weighted at OR=81 with a 12/12 sim-going record and wins in her last two starts over similar distances on Good; five days since her last run is not unusual for Irish handicappers and Cian Quirke is a booking worth noting.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe partners this six-year-old hold-up horse for P J Rothwell — a winner over 24f on Good ground and a 8/14 sim-going record; 16 days since last run and the tp headgear retained.

runners_data.name: Oogum Boogum
runners_data.note: Shane Fitzgerald rides for David Budds on this consistent prominent type — form of P-1323 over similar distances on Good is solid and an OR of 84 leaves him competitive; a 12/15 sim-going record and seven places from those show he runs his race.

runners_data.name: Derby Rock
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type for James Kieran King with no wins from similar going in seven attempts and a recent form string that shows no placing since 2024 — Daniel King rides and the t headgear is unchanged, but the handicap mark looks tight for his level.

runners_data.name: Ardaghs Choice
runners_data.note: Experienced eleven-year-old who is a natural prominent runner by inclination — pushed back into the midfield map because the front positions are over-subscribed, and the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] flag reflects that he is unlikely to secure his preferred slot; 101 days off the track adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Amburana
runners_data.note: Hold-up eight-year-old for Padraig Butler with a fade flag and a recent zero — sim-going record of 6/9 without a win and a form line of 043-70 does not inspire confidence over this trip; Michael Kenneally takes the claim.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: A thirteen-year-old who naturally wants to race up with the pace — the redistribution reflects the reality that eight promoted types cannot all slot in, and at OR=75 with a 14/15 sim-going hit-rate he at least handles the ground well; Sarah Kavanagh's 7lb claim could be relevant if he finds daylight.

runners_data.name: Barely Made It
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator by nature whose true style has pushed him into the midfield map here — the redistribution and [STYLE_FIT=0.90] flag both temper expectations, and a form line of 3P8-59 over similar trips confirms he has not been firing at his best.

runners_data.name: Captain Kate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who races hold-up by habit but carries a [STYLE_FIT=0.90] discount after redistribution — a form string of 666P-P and a sim-going record of 9/13 without a win makes it difficult to frame a winning case for Patrick M O'Brien's mount.

runners_data.name: Eddies Pride
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old veteran with a form line of 0PP-50 and a zero sim-going wins record from 15 attempts — the redistribution from his natural hold-up position and G B Noonan's booking do little to argue against the weight of evidence here.

runners_data.name: Tennesse Boy
runners_data.note: A fade flag accompanies a form line of 020-PP for Robert Tyner's seven-year-old — genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map by the cluster of rear-runners; Phillip Enright takes the mount but the staying trip on Good may not bring out the best.

runners_data.name: Secrecies Of Stone
runners_data.note: An OR=97 prominent runner for Paul Nolan with no jockey declared — a form string of P9-4PP and a 11/15 sim-going record with two wins historically suggests the ability is there, but recent form is a major concern and the missing rider information is a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Chasing Crowns
runners_data.note: A fade flag is the headline concern for this six-year-old hold-up type trained by E Sheehy — form of 390-5P and a 9/12 sim-going record without a win; 16 days between runs and blinkers applied, but the finish fade in a 3m½f chase is a real negative.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Moonshine is the confirmed lone front-runner in this 18-runner handicap chase over 3m½f at Wexford, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good turf. North Of Nashville and Embrace The Day are the most likely horses to track her prominently from the front rank, with Anodandawink and Ladies Well also wanting to be close to the pace. The field contains a significant surplus of prominent-running types — Ardaghs Choice and Fr Gilligansvoyge are genuine front-runners by nature but have been redistributed to midfield on this map because the prominent berths are already full; of those likely to secure a true front-rank position, Midnight Moonshine, North Of Nashville, and Embrace The Day have the strongest claims to the first two or three slots. A single uncontested pace-setter on Good ground over a staying trip, with the race likely to be run at a steady-to-moderate tempo early, strongly favours hold-up or patient mid-to-rear runners who can stalk and produce a sustained late run — closers and stalkers who conserve energy through the first circuit are best placed to exploit any flat finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moonshine Sets Lone Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Moonshine dictates an uncontested, controlled tempo throughout and the race only quickens late.
scenarios.body: Midnight Moonshine establishes a rhythm unchallenged, the early pace is modest, and the field concertinas approaching the final fences; horses who have travelled kindly through the race and jump the final obstacles cleanly are in the best position to score. This shape rewards efficient jumpers with a staying profile who can pick off a tiring leader inside the last half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Grind On
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — North Of Nashville, Embrace The Day, Anodandawink — apply pressure to Moonshine and the race develops a stronger gallop from halfway.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop over 3m½f on Good ground stretches the field out and the race becomes a stamina test from three out; horses with proven staying form and the ability to sustain a gallop to the line are best suited. Embrace The Day's fade flag is a concern, but North Of Nashville's course form and Ladies Well's recent winning run make them dangers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to open the race up for hold-up horses who have been covered up through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Shantou Show and Mistyburn, both genuine hold-up types with respectable course form on Good ground, would be the principal beneficiaries if the front rank burns itself out over the staying trip. Note that several horses mapped in this window — Barely Made It, Captain Kate, Tennesse Boy, and Eddies Pride — are redistributed true hold-up types, and their style fit discount lowers the probability that this shape actually delivers the winner from the back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse And Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or unseated riders disrupt the race shape entirely and a prominent survivor wins on the bridle at a crawl.
scenarios.body: An 18-runner steeplechase over 3m½f carries non-trivial risk of interference through the early fences and a badly disrupted race could gift an opportunistic win to whichever prominent horse jumps cleanly and finds clear air. Ardaghs Choice, despite the redistribution tag, has the experience at OR=77 to capitalise on chaos if allowed to slot into a natural prominent position unchallenged.

watchPoints.text: Midnight Moonshine sets the sole pace but her [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag and a sim-going record of 13/15 without a win in similar conditions means she is likely to be swallowed up late — watch whether the field closes on her from the third-last fence.

The 18-runner field over an early run of steeplechase fences at Wexford creates significant fallers/interference risk — watch the first two fences in particular as crowding in a large jumping field can eliminate multiple fancied runners.

Secrecies Of Stone has no declared jockey at the time of this analysis — if a late booking lands a top conditional or a motivated amateur, her OR=97 rating and two historical wins on similar going could make her a market mover to monitor.

Ladies Well ran only five days ago and carries a strong sim-going record of 12/12 — watch whether the quick turnaround leaves her short of her peak, as her sectional energy reserves over 3m½f will be tested if the pace increases from halfway.

Fr Gilligansvoyge and Ardaghs Choice are both natural prominent types competing for the same limited front-rank slots — watch how early the race settles, because if either secures a prominent position despite the redistribution, their Going and distance profiles make them capable of lasting longer than their odds might suggest.
